en.headline: Subdivided-flat survey finds indoor heat that feels like 52°C
en.dek: CarbonCare InnoLab and the Concerning Subdivided Units Alliance tracked temperatures in 78 inadequate homes and found night-time averages above the Observatory's hot-night threshold, with carers hardest hit.
body: A joint survey released on Sunday found that indoor conditions in Hong Kong's subdivided flats and other inadequate housing reached apparent temperatures as high as 52.21 degrees Celsius during the day, with night-time averages remaining above 29 degrees.

CarbonCare InnoLab and the Concerning Subdivided Units Alliance monitored 86 households across nine districts from 22 June to 12 July, including 78 living in subdivided units or rooftop huts. Daytime average temperatures were 29.93°C and night-time averages 29.42°C, both exceeding the Hong Kong Observatory's 28°C hot-night threshold. The highest recorded indoor temperature was 44.4°C.

Homemakers, who accounted for nearly half of the respondents, reported the greatest impact, with about 80 per cent experiencing dizziness or headaches and many citing high electricity costs for air-conditioning. The groups called for cooling measures to be written into minimum standards for simplified public housing and for more community living rooms with extended opening hours to give residents a cooler refuge.

zh.headline: 劏房調查：室內體感最高達52度 夜間均溫仍逾29度
zh.dek: 低碳想創坊與劏房支援連線監測78個不適切居所，發現日間體感最高52.21度，照顧者受熱及電費雙重壓力最大。
body: 一項周日公布的聯合調查顯示，香港劏房及其他不適切居所的室內體感溫度日間最高達52.21度，夜間平均氣溫仍維持在29度以上。
低碳想創坊與劏房支援連線於6月22日至7月12日在九個地區監測86戶家庭，當中78戶住在劏房或天台屋。日間平均氣溫29.93度，夜間29.42度，均高於天文台28度熱夜門檻；最高室內溫度錄得44.4度。
近半受訪者為家庭照顧者，約八成曾出現頭暈或頭痛等不適，不少人指冷氣電費構成沉重負擔。團體建議將隔熱、通風及必要降溫設備納入簡約公屋最低標準，並增設社區客廳及延長開放時間，讓居民有較涼快的暫避空間。
